Brand guidelines 1.0 · October 2026
Clairix brand guidelines

Calm, clear protection
for everyday people.

Clairix finds hidden cameras, trackers and spyware, and keeps calls and messages private. The brand should feel like the app: quiet, confident and on your side. This page sets out how.

NameClairix, from clair: clear, as in clairvoyant.
Domainclairix.app
PlansClairix Free and Clairix Pro
01 · Concept

The Glint

Shine a light across a room and a hidden camera gives itself away with a single point of reflected light. That glint is the moment the hidden becomes visible. It is what Clairix does, and it is our symbol.

The symbol is a lens seen in light: a ring whose stroke is heavy at the lower left and thins toward an opening at the upper right, where one round point of light sits. Read quickly, it is a C for Clairix. Read slowly, it is a lens catching the light, or an eye that has just noticed something.

1The outer circle sets the size. Everything else is measured from it.
2The counter is a circle shifted toward the opening, so the ring tapers the way light falls across a curved surface.
3Two parallel cuts make the opening. Its width leaves the same clearance on both sides of the Glint.
4The Glint is a true circle on the opening’s axis. It is the only colour in the mark.
02 · Logo

Symbol, wordmark, lockups

The wordmark is set in Inter Display SemiBold, outlined, re-spaced by hand and given round tittles that echo the Glint. Use the horizontal lockup by default. Use the symbol alone once people already know it is us: the app icon, favicons, avatars.

03 · Clear space and minimum size

Give it room

Clear space is measured in G, the diameter of the Glint. Keep at least 2G clear on every side of the symbol, and the wordmark’s x-height clear around the lockups. More is always better.

2G

04 · Misuse

Keep it as drawn

The mark works because it is simple and exact. Use the supplied files and leave them as they are.

05 · Colour

Ink, light and one clear blue

Mostly quiet neutrals, with Clair Blue used the way the Glint is used: once, where it matters. Status colours are softened so a warning informs instead of alarms. Every colour is defined in OKLCH, with its sRGB hex.

06 · Typography

Inter, and only Inter

One family, used with care, reads as confidence. Inter was drawn for screens: a tall x-height, open shapes and clear figures keep it legible at 11 px on a budget phone, and its Display optical size tightens up for headlines. It is free under the SIL Open Font License, so the app, the site and print all use the same files.

Aa

Inter

Interface and body text, 11 to 19 px. Regular 400, Medium 500, SemiBold 600. Tabular figures for numbers that change.

Aa

Inter Display

Headlines from 20 px up. Inter’s display optical size: tighter spacing and finer detail. SemiBold 600.

Aa

JetBrains Mono

Machine values only: MAC addresses, cell IDs, certificate fingerprints. Never for prose or headlines.

07 · Voice and tone

Calm, plain, on your side

People open Clairix when they are worried. Our job is to lower the temperature: say what we found, what it means, and what to do next. We never use fear to sell.

Calm

We state facts at an even pitch. No exclamation marks in alerts. No capitals for emphasis.

Plain

Everyday words. “Tracker”, not “BLE beacon”. Technical detail is one tap away for those who want it.

Honest

We say what we can and cannot know. We never promise total safety, because no one can.

Brief

Short sentences, one idea each. Headlines under eight words, sentences under twenty.

Helpful

Every alert ends in a next step the person can take now.

Respectful

We never blame, never shame, and never assume who is behind a tracker or an app.

What we say, and what we don’t

A tracker is following
A tracker has been near you for 40 minutes. Here’s how to find it.
ALERT! Someone is stalking you!
Room scan is clear
No hidden cameras found in this scan. Check again if you move rooms.
You’re 100% safe. No spies here.
Keylogger keyboard
This keyboard can read what you type. You can switch keyboards in two steps.
Your phone has been hacked. Act now.
Unusual cell tower
A nearby cell tower is behaving unusually. Your Clairix calls stay encrypted.
IMSI catcher detected. Your calls are being intercepted!
Panic wipe
Erase Clairix data on this phone? This can’t be undone.
Nuke everything?
Upgrade to Pro
Pro checks in the background, so you don’t have to remember.
Don’t leave yourself exposed. Upgrade before it’s too late.

Words

We use
  • check
  • found
  • near you
  • private
  • remove
  • turn off
  • encrypted
  • only you
  • here’s how
  • nothing found
We avoid
  • hacker
  • threat actor
  • attack
  • nuke
  • stealth
  • military-grade
  • unhackable
  • 100% secure
  • paranoid
  • act now

Rules for every line

  • What happened, what it means, what to do. In that order, every time.
  • Sentence case everywhere, including buttons and titles.
  • Buttons are verbs: “Scan room”, “Find tracker”, “Remove app”. Never “OK” when something will happen.
  • Numbers as digits, with units: 40 minutes, 3 apps, 2 steps.
  • Name the thing, not the person. “This tracker”, never “your stalker”.
  • Contractions are fine. We sound like a person, not a policy.
08 · Photography and illustration

Daylight, not darkness

Our pictures show the moment after the worry: someone settling into a rental flat, a commuter with a bag on their lap, a friend handing back a phone. Real places, natural light, calm faces. Security, shown as ordinary life going on.

Photography

Do

  • Real people in everyday places: homes, hotels, trains, cafés.
  • Soft daylight, open space, a clear subject.
  • Phones in hand, screens showing real Clairix UI.
  • Diverse ages and backgrounds. Clairix is for everyone.
  • A gentle, slightly cool grade with true skin tones.

Don’t

  • Hooded figures, dark rooms, faces lit by screens.
  • Padlocks, shields, binary code, matrix rain, glitch effects.
  • Eyes peering through blinds, victims, fear, distress.
  • Staged stock poses and heavy filters.
  • Spy gadgets as decoration.

Grade reference: lift shadows toward Ink, keep highlights clean, let one cool tone carry the frame.

Illustration and icons

Built from the same parts as the symbol: circles, arcs and straight cuts on a 24-unit grid. Flat fills from the palette, Clair Blue used once per drawing as the point of light. Icons use a 1.75 px stroke with round caps and joins to match Inter.
